the error exponent of the discrete joint quantization and watermark system is lower bounded by the sum of two terms: the first one, which is a function of the quantization and watermark rates, is the error exponent of a joint quantization system with a perfect attack channel; and the second term, which is a nonnegative function of the attack rate, is the error probability of a private watermarking system with a quantized covertext.

we establish random-coding error exponent lower bounds for the discrete and Gaussian joint watermarking and quantization systems that are positive in the achievable quantization-rate and watermarking-rate region.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a new approach to analyze the error exponent of joint quantization and watermark systems.
the error exponents of the discrete and Gaussian systems are positive in the entire achievable quantization and private-watemarking rate region.

the error exponent of a joint quantization and watermark system with random codes is positive in the interior (in the discrete case) or on the boundary (in the Gaussian case) of the achievable rate region, and is zero outside the region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the error exponent of a joint quantization and watermark system is a function of the joint quantization and the watermarking rate pair.

the error exponent of joint quantization and watermarkting systems is not necessarily zero at the boundary of the achievable rate region, which is a common feature in the error exponent analysis of other communication problems.
the error exponent of the joint system is strictly greater than that of the quantization or watermarking system alone.
